authoring_notes: Authored from the AWS AIP-C01 standard exam guide and official service documentation. modules.title: Task 4.1: Implement cost optimization and resource efficiency strategies.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Track token usage, trim irrelevant history, summarize, compress, set response limits, and prune context __________.

reveal.text: Track token usage, trim irrelevant history, summarize, compress, set response limits, and prune context.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: A long-running assistant’s cost rises because every request includes a very large context → __________

reveal.text: A long-running assistant’s cost rises because every request includes a very large context.

prompts.label: COST LEVERS
prompts.placeholder: Reveal the lever that fits each token-cost symptom. The cheapest optimization is the one that removes work without harming required quality.

cells.lever: Prune/summarize context and keep only needed state
cells.caveat: Do not discard facts required for correctness

cells.symptom: Large stable prefix repeats across requests
cells.lever: Prompt caching where supported and a high-reuse prefix exists
cells.caveat: Caching helps repeated content, not unique prompts

cells.symptom: Many simple requests use an expensive high-capability model
cells.lever: Route/cascade simple work to a cheaper adequate model

cells.symptom: RAG inserts too many low-value chunks
cells.caveat: Over-pruning can remove evidence needed for grounded answers

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Exam trap to avoid: __________

reveal.text: Do not optimize only output tokens while ignoring large repeated input context.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Choose the least expensive model that meets quality and safety requirements, with escalation for harder tasks __________.

reveal.text: Choose the least expensive model that meets quality and safety requirements, with escalation for harder tasks.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: The majority of requests are simple but a small fraction require a premium model → __________

reveal.text: The majority of requests are simple but a small fraction require a premium model.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Key tools/patterns: __________

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Exam trap to avoid: __________

reveal.text: Lowest price per token is not the only cost factor if quality causes retries or failures.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Use batching, concurrency controls, capacity planning, and Provisioned Throughput when utilization patterns justify them __________.

reveal.text: Use batching, concurrency controls, capacity planning, and Provisioned Throughput when utilization patterns justify them.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Predictable sustained traffic needs stable capacity and better throughput economics → __________

reveal.text: Predictable sustained traffic needs stable capacity and better throughput economics.

prompts.label: CAPACITY CHOICES
prompts.placeholder: Reveal which capacity pattern fits the workload shape.

cells.watch: Quotas and shared capacity under spikes

cells.fit: Predictable sustained demand that justifies reserved capacity
Large offline jobs that do not require interactive latency
cells.watch: Not appropriate when the user is waiting synchronously

cells.fit: Smooth bursts and keep downstream components within capacity
cells.watch: Unbounded concurrency can create throttling and retry storms

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Exam trap to avoid: __________

reveal.text: Provisioning fixed capacity for sparse traffic can waste money.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Cache repeated prompts, semantic results, deterministic outputs, or edge responses when freshness and privacy allow it __________.

reveal.text: Cache repeated prompts, semantic results, deterministic outputs, or edge responses when freshness and privacy allow it.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Many requests share a large stable system context and repeated reference text → __________

reveal.text: Many requests share a large stable system context and repeated reference text.

prompts.label: CACHE THE RIGHT THING
prompts.placeholder: Reveal what each cache reuses. Prompt-prefix reuse and semantic-answer reuse are different optimization layers.

cells.reuses: Supported repeated prompt/context prefixes during model invocation
cells.risk: Low reuse or frequently changing prefixes reduce benefit

cells.reuses: A prior answer for a sufficiently similar request
cells.risk: Staleness, privacy, authorization, and similarity-key mistakes

cells.reuses: Expensive retrieval/query results for stable data and safe cache keys
cells.risk: Serving stale or cross-tenant context if invalidation/keying is wrong

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Exam trap to avoid: __________

reveal.text: Do not cache user-specific sensitive output without correct keying and isolation.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Profile each stage and use streaming, parallelization, precomputation, latency-optimized inference, or smaller models where appropriate __________.

reveal.text: Profile each stage and use streaming, parallelization, precomputation, latency-optimized inference, or smaller models where appropriate.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Users complain about slow time-to-first-token and overall response time → __________

reveal.text: Users complain about slow time-to-first-token and overall response time.

prompts.label: FIND THE LATENCY STAGE
prompts.placeholder: Reveal the first optimization to consider for each measured bottleneck.

cells.lever: Tune filters, top-k, indexes, reranking, and network path
cells.trap: Switching the FM does not fix a slow retriever

cells.lever: Streaming, appropriate model choice, inference settings, or latency-optimized options where supported
cells.trap: Do not blame retrieval without a trace

cells.lever: Parallelize independent work, remove redundant calls, and set timeouts
cells.trap: Parallelize only calls that are independent and safe

cells.lever: Profile hops, Region placement, connection reuse, and private/public path choices
cells.trap: Application code micro-optimization will not remove network RTT

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE

reveal.text: Model generation time may not be the only bottleneck; retrieval and tools also matter.

modules.title: Task 4.3: Implement monitoring systems for GenAI applications.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Track operational health, performance traces, FM interactions, and business impact in a coherent observability model __________.

reveal.text: Track operational health, performance traces, FM interactions, and business impact in a coherent observability model.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: A dashboard shows infrastructure uptime but cannot connect application behavior to model calls and business outcomes → __________

reveal.text: A dashboard shows infrastructure uptime but cannot connect application behavior to model calls and business outcomes.

prompts.label: OBSERVABILITY LAYERS
prompts.placeholder: Reveal the signal class and the question it answers. Infrastructure uptime alone is not enough.

cells.examples: Errors, throttles, latency, availability, queue depth
cells.question: Is the system healthy and fast?

cells.examples: Model ID, token usage, stop reason, safety/guardrail outcomes where available
cells.question: How is the model call behaving and costing?

cells.examples: Retrieved chunks, ranking, tool calls, handoffs, per-step latency
cells.question: Which reasoning/data/tool stage caused the result?

cells.examples: Task success, user feedback, groundedness/evaluation results
cells.question: Is the application producing useful outcomes?

cells.examples: API activity, prompt/model version, trace IDs, policy events
cells.question: Can we explain and investigate what happened?

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Exam trap to avoid: __________

reveal.text: Infrastructure metrics alone are not sufficient for a GenAI application.

reveal.text: Track token usage, prompt effectiveness, hallucination/quality indicators, invocation logs, drift, benchmarks, and cost anomalies.
